summary.headline: Archean Q4 FY26 EBITDA fell 34.3% YoY to INR66.4 crore on salt pricing and volume pressure, with the US-Iran conflict and Kutch logistics disruption driving the decline.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 total income was INR304.7 crore, down 9% YoY, with reported EBITDA of INR66.4 crore (21.79% margin) and PAT of about INR29.8 crore. Industrial salt volumes fell 7.2% YoY to 1.1 million tons, with about 120,000 tons of customer deferrals and about 250,000 tons of shipments not completed due to logistics problems. Bromine volumes were about 3,731 tons, up 4% YoY, with realisation up 14% YoY and production back to historical daily rates since mid-February. Management said FY27 bromine growth targets remain 15-20% a year, with a longer-term goal of 40,000 tons, while Acume and Idealis Mudchemie ramp-ups have lagged expectations.

financial_highlights.metric: Cash and bank balances at 31 March
financial_highlights.value: Standalone INR37 crore; consolidated INR55 crore

segments.name: Industrial salt
segments.commentary: Q4 volume 1.1 million tons, down 7.2% YoY; pricing down about 10% YoY but stable QoQ. FY26 sales 4.2 million tons, up 22%, versus an earlier internal estimate of about 4.5 million tons. Contributed 67% of Q4 sales.

segments.name: Elemental bromine
segments.commentary: Q4 volume about 3,731 tons, up 4% YoY and up 53% vs Q3 FY26. Realisation up 14% YoY. Contributed about 32% of Q4 sales (30% per the second statement).

segments.name: Bromine derivatives (Acume Chemicals)
segments.commentary: Q4 sales up nearly 50% YoY; FY26 revenue up nearly 300% YoY to about INR81 crore on about 5,300 tons. Q4 revenue INR23.8 crore on about 1,400 tons. Capacity utilisation about 45%; margins under pressure during ramp-up.

segments.name: SOP
segments.commentary: FY26 volume 644 tons and revenue INR3.49 crore, a very small contributor. Plant trials for the re-engineered product system expected in Q1 FY27, with higher production in H2.

segments.name: Idealis Mudchemie (formerly Oren Hydrocarbons)
segments.commentary: Three plants commissioned in the past 12 months; customer trials ongoing. Gujarat (Mandvi) plant is production-ready but awaiting state approvals. Expects a lean H1 FY27 and a larger ramp in H2. Original INR150 crore revenue target now delayed.

guidance_outlook: Bromine production targeted to grow 15-20% a year, with next milestone of 25,000 tons and then 40,000 tons over time; management said the 25,000-ton level is about 15% above the current run-rate of 50-55 tons per day.
Salt business expected to grow 10-12%, with brine field expansion (6-9 months to complete, then a season to fill ponds) supporting 10-15% capacity growth.
Kutch road works expected to continue until early Q3 FY27, after which fleet distance and turnaround time should normalise.
Management expects full margin recovery as highway works finish, freight and fuel costs ease and the US-Iran conflict subsides; no formal numerical guidance was given.
Idealis Mudchemie: at least two of three plants expected to run at reasonable volume in H2 FY27.
Semiconductor (SiCSem, Odisha): fiscal support agreement signed with GoI; substructure work to start July 2026, with 27-30 months to completion per management's reconciliation.
summary.management_tone: Cautious on near-term earnings and evasive on forward numbers: management repeatedly declined to give pricing ranges, a debt level or profit guidance, and attributed the Q4 decline to external shocks. Confident on the long-term bromine and salt growth story, with the 40,000-ton target and 10-15% salt capacity growth reiterated.

qa_highlights.question: Sanjesh Jain (ICICI Securities): how much did freight and fuel hurt Q4, what are bromine prices for next year, and can bromine return to the historical peak near 5,500 tons a quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Logistics cost rose about INR100-120/ton in February and reached INR200-220/ton by March, a weighted impact of about INR14-15 crore in Q4. Bromine is back at about 55 tons/day, implying roughly 20,000-21,000 tons a year if sustained; the next milestone is 25,000 tons and then 40,000 tons over time.

qa_highlights.question: Sanjesh Jain: what went wrong at Acume and what is the flame retardant plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited longer pharma product development cycles, pricing pressure as an entrant, and bromine supply constraints from Hajipir in Q2-Q3. Actions include a deeper sales team, new products (Zinc Bromide upgrade, PBR 3, two more alkali bromide products in H1 FY27) and process cost work.

qa_highlights.question: Sanjesh Jain: semiconductor milestones and timeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Rajeev Kumar said substructure work starts July 2026; management reconciled to roughly 27-30 months from now to completion.

qa_highlights.question: Aditya Khetan (SMIFS): why are bromine realisations flat versus rising spot prices, and why is FY27 volume growth of 10-15% far below earlier FY26 guidance of 22,000-25,000 tons?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said pricing is driven by about 70% long-term contracts, so realisations lag spot; majority of contracts are now repriced upwards. On volume, it restated the 50-55 tons/day run-rate and a 15% higher FY27 target near 25,000 tons; the management team 'has expanded, not changed'.

qa_highlights.question: Aditya Khetan: what drove the INR13 crore increase in inventory cost in COGS, and what is captive bromine consumption for FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: Unsold finished salt inventory built up in Q4 because deferred orders and logistics constraints prevented shipments; captive bromine consumption figure was not provided and will be emailed.

qa_highlights.question: Avnish Tiwari (Vaikarya): is the bromine supply gap still present and what are the spot versus long-term price levels; can management give EBITDA or breakeven guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Supply on trade routes still trails pre-conflict levels; spot has eased from RMB70,000-80,000 to about US$4-4.5/kg and short-term deal pricing tracks spot. Management declined forward EBITDA, revenue or breakeven guidance.

qa_highlights.question: Rohit Nagraj (360 ONE): bromine price range for next year, timeline to INR150 crore for Idealis, and salt pricing in USD vs INR?
qa_highlights.answer: No bromine price range given. Idealis: about 40-45% of the INR150 crore was expected from Mandvi bentonite, which awaits state approvals; the rest needs retooling; at least two of three plants expected at reasonable volume in H2 FY27. Salt pricing varies by geography: South Asia high-grade commands premiums, while China is more competitive.

capex_capacity: Bromine: management said production is back to historical daily rates of about 50-55 tons per day since mid-February; the 25,000-ton next milestone is about 15% above the current run-rate, with 40,000 tons as the longer-term anchor.
Salt: brine field expansion takes 6-9 months to complete, then a full season to fill ponds before liquor and salt can be drawn; this supports 10-15% salt capacity growth.

Idealis Mudchemie: three plants commissioned in the past 12 months; Gujarat (Mandvi) bentonite plant is production-ready but awaiting state approvals after NCLT-related interpretation issues; Nagri (Andhra Pradesh) plant being retooled for starch, PAC and Fibroseal products; at least two of three plants expected at reasonable volume in H2 FY27.
Acume Chemicals: capacity utilisation about 45% in Q4 during ramp-up; PBR 3 launched and zinc bromide volumes being scaled.
SOP: re-engineered product system and manufacturing process; plant trials expected in Q1 FY27 with higher production in H2 FY27.

SiCSem (Odisha semiconductor): fiscal support agreement signed with Government of India; substructure work targeted from July 2026, with roughly 27-30 months to completion per management's reconciliation.
demand_pricing: Industrial salt Q4 volume 1.1 million tons, down 7.2% YoY; about 120,000 tons deferred due to US-Iran conflict and about 250,000 tons of shipments not completed due to logistics issues.
Industrial salt pricing down about 10% YoY, stable QoQ; FY26 salt sales 4.2 million tons, up 22%, versus an earlier internal estimate of about 4.5 million tons.

Bromine Q4 volume about 3,731 tons, up 4% YoY and up 53% vs Q3 FY26; realisation up 14% YoY; management said majority of bromine long-term contracts have been renegotiated upwards, with no numbers given.

Management said about 70% of bromine business is on long-term annual-priced contracts and 30% on short-term deal-by-deal pricing; spot bromine rose to around RMB70,000-80,000 (about US$8-9/kg) after the crisis and has since eased to about US$4-4.5/kg per management.

Logistics: Kutch road diversion roughly doubled effective distance; Q4 logistics cost increase of about INR200-220 per ton by March, with a Q4 weighted impact of about INR14-15 crore; global freight up 18-20%, industrial fuel up about 50%, coal, sulfur and propanol up 20-30%.

Acume (bromine derivatives) Q4 revenue INR23.8 crore on about 1,400 tons; FY26 revenue about INR81 crore on about 5,300 tons, up nearly 300%; Q4 sales up nearly 50% YoY; margins under pressure during ramp-up.
Idealis Mudchemie original INR150 crore revenue target now delayed; oil and gas demand muted due to Middle East conflict.
risks_watch: Kutch road works expected to run until early Q3 FY27; logistics cost and fleet turnaround remain elevated until then.
Bromine price normalisation after the spike: management says spot has eased to about US$4-4.5/kg, and about 30% of volume is short-term priced.
Salt pricing pressure in distant geographies such as China, with 10% YoY price decline in Q4 and rising competition from new capacity in Australia and the Middle East.
Idealis Mudchemie: Mandvi plant approvals pending with Gujarat authorities; original INR150 crore revenue target delayed with no new timeline.
Acume capacity utilisation about 45%; margin recovery depends on product ramp-up and bromine supply consistency from Hajipir.
Monitor Q1 FY27 SOP plant trials, H1 FY27 Idealis volumes, and the captive bromine consumption figure promised by email.
key_quotes: And therefore, this year has been fairly skewed with headwinds outweighing the positives, resulting in a constant focus on recalibrating the business operations.
The year-on-year decline in EBITDA was largely driven by the drop in pricing or lower pricing realization and lower volume, both of which happened in Industrial Salt.
So we do expect the salt business will continue to grow at 10% to 12%.
I'm going to award you a range as well on bromine pricing.
However, I will -- we really don't give very specific guidance on pricing for reasons you very well understand right -- and therefore I will avoid giving the range as well.
